solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog training ahead of test? It requires careful manipulation

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: An owner drills a puppy before some trial, a task that calls for a delicate touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface keeps you thinking of dog handling, but the manipulation is of strings: a puppeteer's hands work the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the art of working puppets, which depends on careful manipulation of strings or hands.

clue.text: Official caught in tricky situation on the runway?

explanation.surface: A match official gets into a scrape out on an airstrip.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: things done on the runway before take-off are preflight, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Preflight checks and procedures happen on the runway, before the plane takes off.

clue.text: Flatten out gold beneath thin sheet of silver?

parts.note: plate is a thin coating of silver (or other metal), as in silver plate
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A metalworker hammers gold under a thin layer of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatten out' sits comfortably in the metalworking picture, but it is the definition: to plateau is to level off.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prices or growth that plateau stop rising and stay level, as a graph line goes flat.

clue.text: Make charming final piece on organ

parts.note: the end is the final piece
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An organist plays a charming last number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the church instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them liked, to make them charming to others.

clue.text: Providing corrective action in respect of me fizzling out

parts.note: something fizzling out is dying away

explanation.surface: Someone takes steps to rescue their own flagging energy.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the memo-heading word for 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedying something is putting it right, taking corrective action.

clue.text: Summit where clubs vote to accept overseas capital

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
a vote is marked with a cross, X

explanation.surface: At a summit meeting, club delegates vote to admit a foreign capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a political conference, but it is simply a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the highest point of something, its summit.

clue.text: Lesser celeb's monastic life devoid of love

indicators.note: something devoid of a thing lacks it entirely

parts.note: the cloister stands for secluded monastic life
love = nil in tennis, the letter O; removed

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity takes up a celibate monk's life.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A C-lister is a celebrity of the third rank, below the A- and B-list.

clue.text: Fellow almost entirely overwhelmed by daft vernacular

indicators.note: MATE loses its last letter

parts.note: fellow = MATE, short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A man is swamped by a silly way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'almost' trims MATE, 'entirely overwhelmed by' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernacular speech is idiomatic: natural, everyday native language.

clue.text: A plane maybe circling popular race venue

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: An aircraft circles a well-loved racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not an aircraft. AINTREE is the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National horse race is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous horse-racing course, home of the Grand National.

clue.text: Significant time to worry about losing face

indicators.note: the remainder is turned round

explanation.surface: A moment of worry about being humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing face' looks like humiliation, but here the face of a word is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period marked out by some notable event or character, which is what makes the time significant.

clue.text: Protest ignited India towards destruction

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
India is I in the NATO alphabet
on = towards, as in marching on the capital

explanation.surface: A demonstration sparks unrest across India that heads for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word of the protest story turns into its own short piece, strung together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of buildings knocked down, though a sports team can also suffer a demolition.

clue.text: Heading for shelter from conflict in city

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: Refugees flee fighting in a city in search of safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of refugees, but the definition is nautical: to head leewards is to move towards the sheltered side, away from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leewards means towards the lee, the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: It contains stuff from the east, infused with a soy-based sauce

indicators.note: IT holds the rest inside it
in an across clue, read from right to left

parts.note: used as it stands, split to hold the rest

indicators.note: A is added to the reversed stuff

parts.note: to stuff is to RAM, turned round

explanation.surface: A label describes a sauce made with eastern ingredients and soy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun (ingredients) but is the verb: to ram is to stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamari is a Japanese sauce brewed from soybeans, usually with little or no wheat, a specific example of the category.

clue.text: Collection of people having no right to enter university

parts.note: a group is a collection of people

explanation.surface: A crowd of people barred from getting into a university.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'go up' to a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, when you start there.
explanation.definitionFit: To go up is British idiom for starting at, or returning to, university.

clue.text: In part, Republican denies freaking out leader

indicators.note: someone freaking out loses composure, so DENIES loses its order

parts.note: pt is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A Republican partly denies that the leader is losing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' reads as 'partly', but it splits: 'part' is PT and 'In' puts the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a president heads a republic, a company or a club, one of many kinds of leader.

clue.text: Huge fuss around finale of spectacular TV show

indicators.note: the last letter of spectacular

explanation.surface: A spectacular TV show ends in a huge fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacular' looks like praise for the show; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is a reality TV show in which contestants live together under constant filming.

clue.text: Holidaymaker perhaps heading for basically every Indian state, we're told

indicators.note: the first letter of basically

parts.note: Goa, the Indian state, said in a British accent, sounds like goer

explanation.surface: A tourist sets off for pretty much every state in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic (British) accent, in which GOER and GOA sound the same. Goa is famous for its beaches, so the holidaymaker fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachgoer is someone who visits the beach, often on holiday.

clue.text: Singing centrally features in one great new style of music

indicators.note: the middle letter of singing
the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: middle letter of the seven-letter singing

explanation.surface: A song's middle section appears in a great new musical genre.
explanation.walkthrough: Reggaeton is a Latin dance music that began in Puerto Rico, mixing reggae with hip-hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: reggaeton is one particular genre, Puerto Rican dance music with a dembow beat.

clue.text: Pips possibly from fresh limes in a G&T

indicators.note: the letters are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; G&T supplies G and T

explanation.surface: Pips floating out of lime slices in a gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: The pips are not fruit seeds: 'the pips' are the BBC radio beeps marking the hour, a time signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips broadcast on BBC radio on the hour are a time signal.

clue.text: This month, material of mine is available to buy

parts.note: inst. (instant) means 'of this month' in old business letters
ore is the material dug from a mine

explanation.surface: An author announces their new material is on sale this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the pit that ore comes out of.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail idiom: a product 'in store' is stocked on the shop floor, as opposed to online only or coming soon.

clue.text: Horned mammal seen to the south of one cold country

parts.note: C = cold, as on a tap
the eland is an African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope is spotted south of a chilly land.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written backwards to the answer: the mammal comes first in the clue but last in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, and the surface's 'cold' is a nudge: the island nation sits just below the Arctic Circle.

clue.text: Machine part broken by large blockage

indicators.note: a thing broken by something has it forced through the middle

parts.note: a cog is a toothed machine wheel
L = large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A machine component breaks because something big has jammed it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a jammed machine, and a clog is exactly what jams it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a clog in the drain; the verb 'to clog' is to block up.

clue.text: The French tennis great ultimately squanders lead more than once

definitions.note: 'lead more than once' stands for the plural, leads

indicators.note: the last letter of squanders

explanation.surface: A French tennis star throws away a lead repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a sporting advantage, but it is a dog's lead. 'More than once' makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Leashes are dog leads; the plural is signalled by 'more than once'.

clue.text: Dish that's initially covered in a tiny amount of salt

indicators.note: the first letter of that’s

explanation.surface: A recipe dish that is barely seasoned, with only a pinch of salt on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A gratin is itself a dish covered in a crust, so 'covered' suits the kitchen picture while doing the container's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is a dish topped with a browned crust of breadcrumbs or cheese.

clue.text: When power and fury combine, shoot for the stars!

parts.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A motivational slogan: harness your strength and anger and reach high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is easy to read as a mere connective; it supplies AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom standing in for the verb: shooting for the stars is aiming very high, which is what aspiring means.

clue.text: Certain animals, primarily horses included in my analysis info

indicators.note: the first letter of horses
something included in a group is taken inside it

parts.note: cor! = my!, a British exclamation of surprise
data is the information you analyse

explanation.surface: A researcher's notes on some animals, mostly horses, used in their study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!', which is COR in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Chordata is the phylum of animals with a notochord, including all vertebrates.

clue.text: I've nothing more to say about a fancy donut!

indicators.note: DONUT is made into something fancy, rearranged

parts.note: over = about, as in 'arguing over money'

explanation.surface: Someone is struck dumb by an elaborate doughnut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over and out' is radio talk for ending a transmission, hence 'nothing more to say'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Over and out' is the radio sign-off meaning the speaker has finished.

clue.text: Angry and tired, though not at first

explanation.surface: Someone cross and weary, though they weren't to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' for tired is informal: 'my nerves are shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot under the collar means angry.

clue.text: Finest head journalist outsmarted

explanation.surface: The top editor of a paper has been outwitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head journalist' could suggest a first letter; it is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to best a rival is to get the better of them, often by wit.

clue.text: Young relative also thus taken in by good prank periodically

indicators.note: every other letter of prank

explanation.surface: A youngster is also fooled by a harmless practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' means taking every other letter; here the even ones of prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a young male relative, a child's child.
